english_verification.review_scope: Read the A59 ruler and heir lines in local history; checked current country-name localizations and the English mission/event strings for The Grand Masquerade, the Court of Blood, and the Midnight Monarchy. Read actual Markdown chunks from three fixed-revision pages for Korbarid origins, the Dragonwake, Daravan's Folly, Castanorian rule, and the sparse Corvuria history header. This was representative historical and terminology checking, not an exhaustive mission audit. Primary compared all native idea names/descriptions by actual current English localisation key. Source ranges may be locator envelopes; conditional and predecessor idea sets remain separate. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: The Corvuria Wiki history chunk is sparse and marked unfinished in the existing country evidence; the historical outline relies on the actual Korbarid chunks and does not fill gaps from the stub.
No ruler-name conflict is claimed; the article follows the native English history spelling Davan II síl Vivin. Exact Wiki dates and explanations remain limited.
A59's two routes are separate: continuing the vampire storyline blocks Dostanor (Z07); full vampire faction and event reachability was not exhaustively audited.

rationale.campaign_length: A59 has 72 direct mission definitions, some of which may be gated by conditions.
rationale.colonization: Migration and the recovery of Daravan's Folly are not centered on overseas colonization.
rationale.complexity: Vampire estate influence, territorial wars, and a recovery project lasting years overlap.
rationale.dark_story: Blood-feeding, harvesting, and inhumane experiments are substantive parts of the dark narrative.
rationale.difficulty: The campaign requires estate management and several parallel objectives; it was not tested in-game.
rationale.diplomacy: Imperial relations and a network of vampire courts provide diplomatic objectives.
rationale.early_pressure: A poor border kingdom faces pressure from Asheniande and the nearby Empire.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Vampires, blood contracts, and powerful mage rulers drive the main story; artificery is a late-game branch.
rationale.narrative_density: Old family rivalries, the Midnight Court, and regional restoration form a connected story.
rationale.tall_play: Restoring the Folly and developing the capital and production cities occupy much of the campaign.
rationale.trade_economy: River transport, livestock, textiles, and financial thresholds all matter.
rationale.warfare: Asheniande, imperial politics, and expansion south are major campaigns.

identity.appearance: A kingdom ruled by House síl Vivin in 1444.
identity.formation_scope: A59 has its own dedicated mission tree. If it has not embraced vampires and meets the requirements, it may instead form Dostanor (Z07); completing the Grand Masquerade sets a country flag that blocks that decision.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Adopting new ideas depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: The Sapphire Key has long been the badge of authority for the rulers of this land. Originally gifted by Castan I to one of two Foaric chiefs, it enabled them to enter the city of Castonath, the association of which allowed the Raven King to enter Bal Dostan and secure Dostanor during the Dragonwake. Since then, the possession of the Sapphire Key has been a symbol of power, from the Korbarids to Great Cardest to the modern síl Vivin kings. Rulers and dynasties come and go, but the key and the power that its possession grants has endured.

description.text:
For as long as this land has existed, it has been harsh, grim, and cursed.

Daravan the Malignant created the Folly in 669 to fend off the gnollish Drowned Xhaz, drowning the southern half of old Dostanor to no avail for the gnollish survivors, and worse things now threaten our borders. The pogroms committed by the Cardesti and the Korbarids on each other, the Castanorian reconquest of the land by Castan Ebonfrost, the rise of the infamous Corvurian, Nichmer, plunging the continent into war, and finally the White Pestilence - the people here have been hardened and desensitized by cultural traumas over years, and as such, only truly terrifying things can shake a Corvurian..

description.text:
The Order of the Black Thorns is a chivalric order that traces its ancestry back to the Aldresian Crusade. It was the spear-tip of the crusade into the dark heart of Corvuria, which eventually lanced the pustule that caused the pestilence. For this reason, their leader, Lucian síl Vivin, was granted the title of Protector by Jaher, and though he would ultimately disappear, his family and his order would live on, and the Corvurian kings still count the Grand Master of The Black Thorns amongst their titles. Most modern nobles of Corvuria are either a part of or at least had an ancestor who was part of the Order.

The Order of the Black Thorns is known openly for three things: their steadfast, if unorthodox, devotion to Nerat, their brutal and effective skills in war, and their unquestioning loyalty to the síl Vivin kings. Whenever Corvuria is threatened, whether by horrific monsters, terrible undead, or a simple recalcitrant peasant, the Order responds in the same manner: ‘Obliterate, with extreme prejudice.’ Many villages have been left burned to the ground in the wake of a Black Thorn Tribunal, and as such, peasants are quick to denounce their rebellious fellows to prevent their village from becoming the site of the next tribunal.

description.text:
- King Daran V síl Vivin-Arannen, in response to criticisms by mages within his court about the overuse of magic to boost agricultural productivity of the land. The mages in question subsequently vanished.

The power and primacy of kings within Corvuria, be they Corvurian, Korbarid, or otherwise, have always been extremely strong. While many other realms, such as Lorent, Dameria, and Wex, at times need to be cautious of upsetting powerful vassals and always must be cognizant of their rights, in Corvuria, the law is clear: the nobility have no enshrined rights except those granted to them by the Holder of the Sapphire Key, and dissent is treason. This temperament became more and more common outside Corvuria in the period of the Age of Witch-Kings, being adopted and maintained by the Arannese even after their subjugation of Corvuria in the 1600s.

description.text:
Despite the utter dominance of royal power within Corvuria, it is a truly idiotic monarch who would not provide an avenue for advice to be given, and after all, as Queen Celadora once said, “We may die tomorrow, so we’ll drink today.”

A tradition carried over from the Roilsardi crusaders who became the modern Corvurian nobility, the masquerade is a tradition at the heart of the functioning of the state. It is here that all Corvurians, rich and poor, old or young, can intermingle, indulge, and debase themselves freely without fear. Indeed, this is the only chance commoners have to mingle with the nobility. Hosting a grand masquerade is a great honour, solely held to the few nobles who have the king's ear, and those who host the masquerades refresh themselves from such fine conversation and gain new allies or rekindle old ones. Of course, there are some who pointed out that it's always the same families who hold these masquerades, and it always leads to them accruing more power and influence than before.

'Pointed out' being the operative word.

description.text: Land and laborers are equally poor here, and the only way we can get any richer is to work them both to the bone. Despite the soil being volcanic in nature, the interplay of such strong historic royal prerogatives, the frequent threat of raids from the Folly by gnolls, and holdovers from the effect of the White Pestilence have forced the population to become rather effective farmers and laborers out of necessity. For if they were not so, they would not be so.

description.text:
…For example, investment in logging, mining, and riverine infrastructure along the Carnvord and Dostanesck rivers. With ample resources provided by our Corvurian lands, ably extracted by peasants, and transported to factories in Arannen, I am confident that our realm will be able to cement itself as a leading industrial power. Industrial costs would be lower if it were possible to build factories within Corvuria itself, but the comparative lack of literacy amongst the simpleton workforce as well as… more esoteric concerns render that politically impractical for the time being..."

- Magister Ostan of Varlosen, in his essay 'A Survey of our Corvurian Lands', to Ostan IV síl Vivin-Arannen, 1801

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid if you dislike estate thresholds, pressure from powerful neighbors, or a dark narrative that treats subjects as a food source.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Stabilize the frontier through diplomacy, military strength, and economic development, then manage estate power to unlock the Grand Masquerade while pursuing territorial, magical, and financial requirements for the Folly's recovery.
player_overview.overview: Corvuria begins under House síl Vivin, with vampire nobles already entrenched in the state. First defend the frontier and settle the rivalry with Asheniande; then use the Grand Masquerade and the Court of Blood to institutionalize the power of the Night's Nobility. At the same time, restore the blighted Folly and develop waterways and cities. This is a campaign of gothic court politics alongside long-term reconstruction.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy gothic vampires, court intrigue, mage rulers, and long-term reconstruction.
signature_features: A Vampire estate, the Midnight Monarchy, and a powerful vampire mage ruler available only under specific conditions.
A dynastic feud with Asheniande, imperial politics, and the Dark Legion.
A staged restoration of Daravan's Folly that is about more than conquest.
player_overview.tagline: Join a poor border kingdom to its vampire nobility, build a Midnight Court, and restore the cursed Folly.

reasons: Vampire politics gives the country a distinctive identity and mechanics.
Restoring the Folly creates a long-term objective beyond conquest.
Dynastic feuds and imperial diplomacy create a coherent story.
warnings: The Grand Masquerade and an immortal ruler have demanding prerequisites.
Completing the vampire storyline removes eligibility to form Dostanor.

positive_indicators: Restoring the Folly in stages and resettling its population.
Repairing waterways and the urban economy.
Border fortifications can protect some residents.
values.rationale: The capital mission narrative treats ordinary residents as blood livestock for vampires. Completing missions related to Asheniande triggers a harvest event that damages Ashfield's development and leaves it severely devastated; late-game text also permits inhumane experiments. Restoring the Folly, waterways, and cities brings genuine public benefit. The assessment is based on specific harms, not vampire identity, monarchy, or warfare.
red_flags: The narrative treats residents as blood livestock for the Night's Nobility, with the state complicit.
The Ashfield harvest event causes severe devastation and loss of development.
Mission text supports inhumane artificery experiments.
